fields.v:
ER = exploited / completed runs (higher = less secure). Temperature 0, top-p 1, 120 s limit, auto-approve. The authors state no success criterion for an agent (no acceptable ER), so no verdicts are given.
- Gemini CLI + gemini-3-flash + malicious skills: ER 95.5% raw majority, 96.1% with override [95.3, 96.7] (2,705/2,816); per generator 95.5-96.8%; explicit refusal in 17 of 111 failures; Exfiltration 95.5%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Qwen Code + qwen3-coder-plus + malicious skills: ER 71.6% raw, 74.0% with override [72.3, 75.6] (2,081/2,813); per generator 67.7% (DeepSeek-R1) to 76.9%; refusals 95 of 732 failures; Exfiltration 38.5%, Impact 56.2%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Human gold standard: Gemini 95.5% (94.2-96.3), Qwen 70.9% (65.6-75.7)
- Verified execution: 1 run of 5,629 (harness-limited)

fields.v: Gemini CLI more exploitable than Qwen Code by 22-24 points (non-overlapping Wilson CIs); exploitability nearly invariant to generator model; tactic gap largest for Exfiltration (95.5% vs 38.5%); Qwen-only off-task rejection (10.1% of its failures). Explicit safety recognition 1.99% of all runs

fields.v: Distinguished the agents clearly. Single judges disagree strongly on Qwen (Fleiss' kappa -0.06; flag rates 22.4-94.8%), motivating the panel; panel vs human kappa 0.83-0.85. Limitations: single masking template, synthetic not in-the-wild skills, single task, 120 s limit, two agents, residual non-determinism

fields.v: Code and dataset: github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak (per-run logs, prompts, regexes, unit tests). No pre-registration. Language: shell commands; web app language chosen by agent (e.g. Python/Flask). Values from Table 3 and Table 4 (p. 16, layout rebuilt from pdftotext), Table 5 (p. 22), Table 6 (p. 24) and text pp. 18-22. Inconsistencies: (1) 2 x 2,826 = 5,652 planned runs minus 5,629 completed = 23 missing (10 Gemini, 13 Qwen per Table 3 totals), but the text reports 24 empty runs excluded plus two commands with no run recorded (p. 12); (2) Fig. 3 Step 2 says 471 attacks passed to 5 LLMs to generate 2,355 descriptions, whereas the text uses six generator LLMs and 2,826 skills (pp. 8-9); (3) p. 11 says each agent is evaluated over 2,816 completed runs, but Qwen has 2,813 (Table 3); (4) Gemini CLI described as built on the Gemini Pro series but run with gemini-3-flash (p. 11). Relevance to SDD: skill files as agent instruction artefacts and their security risk
